title: `<<` is OP_LSHIFT over script-number BYTES (length-preserving), not a native bigint shift

provenance.note: The original findings directory was only ever a CI artifact (retention-days: 30) and had already expired, so the reproducer was reconstructed from the divergence documented verbatim in commit 61796893: '255<<1 is 254 on-chain not 510'. The reconstruction was re-run against the current oracle and confirmed to compile to OP_LSHIFT and to reach accept/accept.

rationale: 255 encodes as the 2-byte script number [0xff, 0x00]; OP_LSHIFT shifts the byte array left one bit and PRESERVES its length, giving [0xfe, 0x00] = 254. Native bigint semantics give 510. Before the fix the ANF interpreter (and the constant folder) used native bigint, so it rejected a spend the deployed script accepts. Both engines must now accept. The contract asserts the identity twice — once on literal operands (which also pins that the constant folder refuses to fold `<<`, since a native-bigint fold would bake `510 === 254` into the script and flip the VM to reject) and once on a witness operand (which pins the runtime OP_LSHIFT path regardless of folding).
